stories.headline: Anthropic tested Claude on three real hacks to see what it could do
stories.blurb: Anthropic ran Claude through three actual cybersecurity incidents — a leaked API key, a compromised server, and a supply chain attack — to see if the model could investigate and respond like a security analyst. Claude handled basic triage but struggled with multi-step reasoning and deciding when to escalate. The company is publishing the eval framework so other teams can test their own models.
stories.why_it_matters: First public benchmark using real incidents instead of synthetic CTF-style challenges.
stories.original_headline: Investigating three real-world incidents in our cybersecurity evaluations

stories.headline: Google's new Gemini model can watch a room and tell robots what to do
stories.blurb: Gemini Robotics ER 2 watches video feeds, figures out what needs doing, and coordinates multiple robots to handle tasks together. It can reason about real-world scenes and decide which robot should do what—like directing one bot to clean while another fetches supplies.
stories.why_it_matters: Robots can now understand context from video and work together without pre-programmed choreography.
stories.original_headline: Gemini Robotics ER 2: powering robotics with video understanding, task orchestration, and multi-robot collaboration

stories.headline: Apple is planning to charge power users for more AI
stories.blurb: Tim Cook told investors Apple will offer 'upgrade possibilities on iCloud Plus' to let people use Apple Intelligence and the new Siri beyond whatever free limits exist. No pricing or timing yet, but Cook said he expects people will 'want to use it a lot.'
stories.why_it_matters: Apple just confirmed it's building a paid tier for AI — following OpenAI and Anthropic's playbook.
stories.original_headline: Tim Cook hints at iCloud Plus tier for AI power users

stories.headline: Amazon's custom chip business just hit $25 billion a year
stories.blurb: Amazon Web Services now pulls in over $25 billion annually from its custom-designed chips—Graviton for general computing and Trainium/Inferentia for AI workloads. That makes AWS one of the world's largest chip companies by revenue in just a decade, competing directly with Nvidia and Intel by offering cheaper, faster cloud instances to customers who train and run models.
stories.why_it_matters: Cloud providers are now chip giants, which reshapes who controls AI infrastructure costs and performance.
stories.original_headline: How Amazon became one of the world’s top chip companies in a decade
